faqs.question: What is a Nanosurf Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: It's a bespoke AFM system engineered specifically to an application — Nanosurf's engineering and development team designs the sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry around the measurement requirement rather than supplying a catalogue product.

faqs.question: How large and heavy a sample can be measured?
faqs.answer: One documented implementation carries samples up to 500 kg, measuring up to 540 × 1500 × 210 mm on a 785 × 1950 mm platform. Nanosurf states virtually no restrictions on sample weight, size, and geometry.

faqs.question: What noise levels are achievable?
faqs.answer: Below 0.75 Å with the NaniteAFM 110 µm scan head on the extra-large stage, and below 0.40 Å with the Flex-Mount scan head on the XYZΦ stage, both in a quiet environment.

faqs.question: Which scan heads are used?
faqs.answer: Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research-grade scan heads, with tip-scanner technology preserving scanner performance on heavy samples.

faqs.question: How many axes of movement are available?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 degrees of freedom, with the stage designed to reach any position on the sample.

faqs.question: Can curved surfaces be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tiltable scan head combined with multi-axis stage freedom addresses highly polished concave and convex surfaces.

faqs.question: Are these systems cleanroom compatible?
faqs.answer: Yes. Systems are designed to ISO 6 cleanroom compliance, with all materials and components cleanroom certified and assembly carried out in a clean environment.

faqs.question: What safety systems are included?
faqs.answer: A programmable logic controller ensures safe operation, executing safe torque off if safe limited speed is exceeded, the emergency stop is pressed, or an AFM cantilever is lost.

faqs.question: Can the system integrate into factory processes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation solutions go beyond simple measurement series to factory-scale process integration, including MES.

faqs.question: How is performance guaranteed before delivery?
faqs.answer: Detailed system models and performance simulations including environmental factors — acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration — verify that requirements are met by the final system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, SMM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical properties.

faqs.question: What software runs these systems?
faqs.answer: Nanosurf C3000/CX control software, with a scripting interface handling everything from small measurement automation series to full-scale MES integration.

faqs.question: How does the engagement process work?
faqs.answer: It begins with an exploratory meeting to discuss the application. Nanosurf's engineering and development team then works iteratively with your team to design the system around the requirement.

faqs.question: How is this different from buying a Flex-Mount or NaniteAFM?
faqs.answer: Those are products configured to an application. An Industrial Solution is an engineering project — stage, mount, geometry, cleanroom compliance, safety systems, and automation all designed to a requirement no standard configuration meets.

faqs.question: What is the price of a Nanosurf Industrial Solution in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing follows the engineering scope. Get in touch and Inkarp will arrange the application scoping conversation that defines it.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of Nanosurf Industrial Solutions in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Nanosurf in India, providing application scoping, engineering coordination, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: A 500 kg sample. Two metres of travel. Noise under 0.75 Å.
longForm.heroLead: That stage is real and it was built. Over 2 metres long, 1.45 metres wide, weighing more than 2 tonnes — one of the largest AFM stages ever constructed, on air bearings with drive belt and stepper motor positioning, carrying samples up to 500 kg while holding noise below 0.75 Å. It exists because someone needed it. That's the proposition here: Nanosurf's engineering and development team works with yours to understand the requirement and iteratively design an AFM system around it — sample stage, scan head mount, and system geometry designed to the sample, regardless of size, weight, or curvature. Mountable versions of the FlexAFM and DriveAFM research scan heads supply the measurement performance, with tip-scanner technology preserving that performance even on heavy samples. Up to five axes of freedom reach any position on any sample. Before delivery, detailed system models and performance simulations account for acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration, so the requirements are met on arrival rather than discovered afterwards. ISO 6 cleanroom compliance and PLC-governed safety come as part of the design where the application demands them.

sections.title: System Optimization Before Delivery
body: AFM is environmentally sensitive: acoustic noise, temperature variation, and floor vibration all perturb nanoscale measurement.

Detailed system models are built, so the system is modelled rather than assumed to perform in the intended environment. Performance simulations include environmental factors, so the site's real conditions are part of the simulation rather than an unknown.

Requirements are verified at delivery — Nanosurf's stated aim is that all requirements are met by the final system upon delivery. Below 0.75 Å on a 2,250 kg stage carrying 500 kg samples is what the modelling is for, moving risk off the customer by engineering environmental performance in advance rather than discovering it during commissioning.

faqs.question: What is Alphacen 300 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tip-scanning atomic force microscope for large and heavy samples, used in precision optics metrology, surface roughness measurement, industrial quality control, and large substrate characterization.

faqs.question: What sample size and weight can it handle?
faqs.answer: Samples up to 300 × 300 mm in size and up to 45 kg in weight, with a 50 mm z approach stage for thick samples.

faqs.question: Why does tip-scanning matter for large samples?
faqs.answer: The tip moves rather than the sample, so imaging quality holds regardless of sample size or weight — the sample's mass stops affecting scan performance.

faqs.question: What scan head does it use?
faqs.answer: The Flex-Mount scan head, based on proven research scan head technology from Nanosurf's FlexAFM, with a flexure-based tip design.

faqs.question: What scan range does it offer?
What controller does the system use?
faqs.answer: A 24-bit CX controller — Nanosurf's most advanced AFM controller, offering fast and precise control over the scan process.

faqs.question: Is vibration isolation included?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dedicated acoustic enclosure minimizes external noise and vibrations as part of the system.

faqs.question: Which AFM modes are available?
faqs.answer: Static, lateral, dynamic, and phase imaging; C-AFM, SSRM, PFM, EFM, KPFM, and MFM for electrical properties; force spectroscopy, modulation, and mapping for mechanical; plus lithography and nanomanipulation, EC-AFM, and SThM.

faqs.question: Is Scanning Microwave Microscopy available?
faqs.answer: SMM isn't listed in Nanosurf's published mode set for this system, though it appears on the Flex-Mount and Industrial Solutions pages. Confirm availability at configuration if SMM is required.

faqs.question: Can samples larger than 300 mm be measured?
faqs.answer: Yes, through customization — the Alphacen 300 Flex serves as the basis for custom-engineered solutions accommodating samples beyond 300 mm.

faqs.question: Can sample rotation be added?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rotation axes are customizable on both the sample positioning system and the scan head, useful where consistent feature alignment is needed.

faqs.question: Do cantilevers need manual alignment?
faqs.answer: No. Self-aligning cantilevers remove the manual alignment step.

faqs.question: Can measurements be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes. Automation scripts are customizable beyond the built-in options in the AFM software, and the system integrates into larger automation concepts with support from Nanosurf's Automation Software Solutions team.

faqs.question: How is Alphacen 300 different from Flex-Mount?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 Flex is a complete standard system — Flex-Mount scan head, CX controller, and acoustic enclosure, with a defined 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg sample capability. Flex-Mount is the scan head alone, requiring a stage to be specified or built around it.

faqs.question: How is it different from a full Industrial Solution?
faqs.answer: Alphacen 300 is a standard product deliverable without an engineering project. Industrial Solutions are bespoke systems engineered to requirements no standard configuration meets, including cleanroom compliance, PLC safety, and stages carrying up to 500 kg.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Numeric system specifications are published in the Alphacen 300 Flex brochure — Inkarp can provide it on request.

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the mode set, automation requirements, and any customization needed.

longForm.heroHook: 45 kg on the stage, 300 × 300 mm of sample, and a standard system you can order today.
longForm.heroLead: Large-sample AFM usually means one of two things: a scan head that needs a stage designed around it, or a full bespoke engineering project with a scoping phase before anything is quoted. Alphacen 300 Flex is neither. It's a complete, standard system — Flex-Mount scan head, CX controller, dedicated acoustic enclosure — that handles samples up to 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg out of the box, with a 50 mm z approach stage so thick samples mount without difficulty. The performance comes from proven parts. The tip-scanner design means imaging quality holds regardless of sample size or weight, because the tip moves and the sample doesn't. The flexure-based scanner from Nanosurf's FlexAFM delivers flat, linear scanning at 100 µm range. The CX controller is Nanosurf's most advanced, giving fast and precise control over the scan process. The acoustic enclosure handles external noise and vibration as part of the system. And when the requirement outgrows it, the same system becomes the basis for a custom solution — additional translation or rotation axes on the sample positioning system and the scan head alike.

sections.description: Alphacen 300 product information: sample capability, scan performance, and customization scope.
body: A complete standard system: Not a scan head requiring a stage — a full AFM system ready for large and heavy samples.
Samples up to 300 × 300 mm and 45 kg: Large-format and heavy workpieces measured directly.
50 mm z approach stage: Thick samples mount without hassle rather than requiring workarounds.
Flex-Mount scan head: Tip-scanner design enabling high-performance imaging regardless of sample size or weight.
Proven FlexAFM scanner technology: Flexure-based tip design giving flat and linear scanning, high resolution, and stable operation.
100 µm scan range: Full research-grade scan area retained in the industrial format.
24-bit CX controller: Nanosurf's most advanced AFM controller, offering fast and precise scan process control.
Dedicated acoustic enclosure: External noise and vibration minimized as part of the delivered system.
Self-aligning cantilevers: Cantilever alignment handled by design rather than by operator adjustment.
Top and side view camera: Integrated sample observation.
Six electrical modes plus EC-AFM and SThM: Broad characterization range covering electrical, mechanical, and thermal properties.
Customizable automation scripts: Automation extends beyond the built-in options in the AFM software.
Integration into larger automation concepts: Nanosurf's Automation Software Solutions team supports industry 4.0 workflow integration.
Basis for custom-engineered solutions: Sample rotation, additional axes, and samples beyond 300 mm accommodated through customization.
